The register holds 138 findings (1 critical, 37 major, 63 minor, 37 notes) and 2 positions, 115 negative results and 58 unverified items. It is an index and a summary, never the only record: every row points to the dossier section that states it in full, and the dossier's text governs where the two differ.

\paragraph{Numbering.} The rows are numbered by severity and, within a severity, by subject. \code{R1} to \code{R136} were fixed when the register was first published. Rows added later (\code{R137} onward, from the dossier on the obligations) are numbered after them and shown at the end of their severity group, so that no earlier number changes; within a group, the order by subject therefore holds for the earlier rows only.

\paragraph{Revisions.} The object of the review is leanerVM \code{main} at \code{b435631}; leanVM at the pin \code{a386121f}. Library citations name their revision: old pins ArkLib \code{dca90385}, CompPoly \code{3468b38c}, Clean \code{93c9d1ef}, VCVio \code{f9dc47d9} (those of \code{b435631}); new pins after \code{144c5aa} ArkLib \code{7653a901}, CompPoly \code{572f9973}, Clean \code{42fe4b26}, VCVio \code{a4232d08}. Blueprint line numbers are at \code{b435631} (they are $+4$ at \code{HEAD} after line 51). Lean probe outputs are at the old pins unless a row says otherwise.

\paragraph{Status column.} \emph{cited-checked}: a citation check (the dossiers \code{verify-gt-*}) covered the row's citations; corrections it made are applied and marked \enquote{corrected by the check}. \emph{probe-run}: a Lean or Python probe that ran supports it (at the old pins unless stated). \emph{paper}: the argument is a reading or a proof on paper only. \emph{unverified}: the dossier says a part is unverified. Several tags may apply; the text in parentheses says which part.

\paragraph{Merging.} A finding stated by two or more dossiers is one row that cites every dossier and shows each dossier's severity; the row sits at the highest. Findings that are merely related are separate rows. Where dossiers disagree, each position is a row (\cref{sec:reg-disagreements}). Two rows are not findings but positions of one dossier that another dossier's finding contradicts; they carry no severity and sit beside the row they dispute.

\section{The register of findings}\label{sec:reg-findings}

Columns: the row's number; its short name; its severity as the dossiers give it (merged rows show each dossier's); its subject; where it is stated in full (dossier and section or finding heading, with the finding box of this report where one states that dossier section); its classification as the dossier gives it (--- for a finding about the code, the status, a source, or where the dossier gives none); the status of its evidence. The claim, the decisive evidence and the proposed change of every critical and major row follow the first table (\cref{sec:reg-claims}); for the minor rows and the notes they are in the dossier section named. \subsection{Claim, evidence and proposed change of the critical and major rows}\label{sec:reg-claims}

For each critical and major row, in the register's order: the claim, the decisive evidence and the proposed change, as the register gives them. The full text, with the passages as they stand and as proposed, is in the dossier section the row names (\cref{tab:reg-major}).

\begingroup\sloppy
\par\medskip\noindent\textbf{R1.}\enspace\textbf{The existential forms of round-by-round knowledge soundness carry no knowledge content}\enspace{\small\textsf{\color{critical}(critical)}}\par\nopagebreak
\fhead{Claim} ArkLib's round-by-round extractor is any function, so an extractor that picks a witness by classical choice makes the verifier deciding any relation's language knowledge sound at error 0. Theorems in the existential forms (\texttt{piop\_\allowbreak{}rbr\allowbreak{}Knowledge\allowbreak{}Soundness\_\allowbreak{}exists}, the sketches of Layers 9 and 10) are soundness statements only; the spine's named form is adequate only with a compiled extractor.
\fhead{Evidence} ArkLib \texttt{Security/\allowbreak{}Round\allowbreak{}By\allowbreak{}Round.\allowbreak{}lean:\allowbreak{}77-\allowbreak{}86,\allowbreak{} 118-\allowbreak{}123} at \code{dca90385}; probe \code{Extractors} (\code{chooser_sound}, exit 0, old pin)
\fhead{Proposed change} state every interface in the named (\code{With}) form with a compiled extractor checked by a \code{def} without \code{noncomputable}; change \code{:239}, \code{:1084}, \code{:1333} (lib-arklib.md §G.1)

\par\medskip\noindent\textbf{R2.}\enspace\textbf{The bus seam admits statements the deployed table sumcheck cannot serve}\enspace{\small\textsf{\color{major}(major)}}\par\nopagebreak
\fhead{Claim} \code{Seam.bus} accepts any number of linear claims, terms of one table at unrelated points, terms on any table, and a degree bound written as a clause on the statement. Round-by-round knowledge soundness quantifies over every input statement, so the deployed table-sumcheck verifier cannot be proved complete and sound against it without guards (degree, claim count, one point per table) that leanVM does not have; over the seam the error on \code{ξ} is unbounded.
\fhead{Evidence} \texttt{Spine/\allowbreak{}Seams.\allowbreak{}lean:\allowbreak{}130-\allowbreak{}134,\allowbreak{} 175-\allowbreak{}181} at \code{b435631}; probes \texttt{Seam\allowbreak{}Bus\allowbreak{}Shape.\allowbreak{}lean}, \texttt{Seam\allowbreak{}Bus\allowbreak{}Member.\allowbreak{}lean} (exit 0 per the dossier)
\fhead{Proposed change} give \code{BusOut} the shape of the Rust's \code{BusVerify} (\code{leaf.rs:849-860}): one point, forms per side and sumcheck table with the degree in the type, three totals, column claims; smallest fix: make \code{VirtualTerm.poly} a subtype within the degree bound (gt-table-pub.md §8; code-spine.md §F)

\par\medskip\noindent\textbf{R3.}\enspace\textbf{The real bus phase can fill the spine's bus slot; the seam's surplus generality burdens only the table phase}\enspace{\small\textsf{\color{note}(position)}}\par\nopagebreak
\fhead{Claim} The deployed bus phase's output is expressible as a \code{BusOut I} (five linear and five column claims for leanVM), it is perfectly complete (given the side conditions of R43), and a knowledge state function exists. \code{Seam.bus} admits statements the bus phase never emits, but gt-bus calls that ``a burden on the table phase's completeness'', met by ``a table phase written over the terms' own points'', and finds nothing required by the spine that matters.
\fhead{Evidence} gt-bus.md §E.1-E.4 (paper)
\fhead{Proposed change} none proposed beyond the side conditions and the order of the linear claims

\par\medskip\noindent\textbf{R4.}\enspace\textbf{The spine's completeness cannot carry an error, and Flock may need one}\enspace{\small\textsf{\color{major}(major)}}\par\nopagebreak
\fhead{Claim} \texttt{Component.\allowbreak{}Complete} is perfect completeness, while ArkLib composes completeness with additive errors (proved at both pins); acceptance test 20 charges the Flock prover's failure at \code{r_eq = 1} to \code{flockError}, a soundness error.

\par\medskip\noindent\textbf{R5.}\enspace\textbf{The declared error is unconstrained: the knowledge theorem has content only with a bound on \code{piopError}}\enspace{\small\textsf{\color{major}(major)}}\par\nopagebreak
\fhead{Claim} \code{piopError} is whatever each phase declares; five phases that draw a challenge, check nothing and declare error 1 inhabit \code{Phases.Security} for the toy, and both master theorems hold of them. The blueprint's only bound, \code{piopError_le}, takes an argument (\code{s}) that the spine's \code{piopError} does not.
\fhead{Evidence} \texttt{Spine/\allowbreak{}Compose.\allowbreak{}lean:\allowbreak{}149}; \texttt{To\allowbreak{}Ark\allowbreak{}Lib/\allowbreak{}Component.\allowbreak{}lean:\allowbreak{}66,\allowbreak{} 148}; blueprint \code{:318}, \code{:1130}; probe \code{P4Junk.lean} (\code{piopError_junk}, old pins)

\par\medskip\noindent\textbf{R6.}\enspace\textbf{The composition over the prover's announced sizes is unspecified}\enspace{\small\textsf{\color{major}(major)}}\par\nopagebreak
\fhead{Claim} The sizes are the prover's and admissibility is the verifier's check, but the per-instance theorems bound one size vector each, \texttt{verify\_\allowbreak{}iff\_\allowbreak{}compiled} quantifies \code{∃ s}, and ArkLib's fixed \code{ProtocolSpec} cannot express a schedule that depends on a first message. A union over the admissible sizes costs about \code{2^34}; the \code{Q · max ε} Fiat–Shamir bound needs the sizes inside the hashed statement of one protocol.
\fhead{Evidence} blueprint \code{:316}, \code{:1218-1221}, \code{:1226-1227}, \code{:1326-1328}; \texttt{cpu/\allowbreak{}mod.\allowbreak{}rs:\allowbreak{}130-\allowbreak{}178}; \texttt{verifier.\allowbreak{}py:\allowbreak{}1372-\allowbreak{}1379}

\par\medskip\noindent\textbf{R7.}\enspace\textbf{The GKR layer sumcheck is the normalized variant; the blueprint gives it the wrong degree, the wrong error and no definition}\enspace{\small\textsf{\color{major}(major)}}\par\nopagebreak
\fhead{Claim} Each deployed GKR round sends a degree-4 cofactor (four elements on the wire, the constant coefficient derived through the equality factor); the running claim is the cofactor's value and the layer's final check has no equality factor. The blueprint says degree 5 and error \code{5/|E|}, and Layer 4 defines only the plain variant, so a verifier built as written rejects every Rust proof or is a different verifier.

\fhead{Proposed change} define both sumcheck variants in Layer 4 by name; \code{4/|E|} per GKR round in \code{gkrError} and the tracker (gt-bus.md G1)

\par\medskip\noindent\textbf{R8.}\enspace\textbf{The GKR last-layer rounds cost \code{5/|E|} each, as the blueprint says}\enspace{\small\textsf{\color{note}(position)}}\par\nopagebreak

\fhead{Claim} Both verifiers draw a combiner after the roots and after every layer, the last included; the blueprint says one per layer. Harmless in the oracle model, but after Fiat–Shamir the extra squeeze changes every later challenge.

\par\medskip\noindent\textbf{R10.}\enspace\textbf{Layer 5's generic GKR cannot be appended in the bus phase and cannot carry the zerocheck clause}\enspace{\small\textsf{\color{major}(major)}}\par\nopagebreak
\fhead{Claim} The GKR's oracles are the leaf tables, but a phase's one oracle is the stack; carrying the GKR along that map needs ArkLib's context lifting, whose completeness and knowledge soundness are admitted at the pin. And the appended state function cannot carry a clause (the zerocheck) that changes with the GKR's own challenges.

\par\medskip\noindent\textbf{R11.}\enspace\textbf{The table sumcheck's tables are not distinguished from the instance's other tables}\enspace{\small\textsf{\color{major}(major)}}\par\nopagebreak
\fhead{Claim} Layer 3 makes the six shared columns tables of the instance, and Layer 7 takes \code{τ_max} and the final message's width over every table: at least 16 rounds and 110 values, where leanVM runs \code{τ_max} rounds over the six opcode tables (as few as 3) and sends 104 values; \texttt{verify\_\allowbreak{}iff\_\allowbreak{}compiled} would then fail.

\par\medskip\noindent\textbf{R12.}\enspace\textbf{The public-input theorems are about a verifier none of the three executable verifiers runs; the debt is assigned to Layer 12, which cannot pay it}\enspace{\small\textsf{\color{major}(major)}}\par\nopagebreak
\fhead{Claim} The specification checks each limb; the Rust verifier, the Python verifier and the recursion guest check one combined equation \texttt{c₀ + y·c₁ =\allowbreak{} (\allowbreak{}1+r)·w₀ + r·w₁} and pool the scalars sent. That is a different oracle verifier, so Layer 12's compilation theorem cannot hold with a Rust-faithful \code{verify} and cannot detect the difference with a per-limb one (its fixture is an honest proof).

The earlier review's ``each of five wrong verifiers breaks a stated theorem'' is false of the merged code, and the status repeats it.

\fhead{Proposed change} pool the values sent (\code{pooledFrom}), which makes the check load-bearing (its removal and weakening are then refuted, §C.6, §C.7); reword blueprint \code{:1035-1037}; strike status \code{:440}; add the refutations as tests (code-pubinput.md §G.1)

\par\medskip\noindent\textbf{R14.}\enspace\textbf{Layer 9's Flock interface consumes the eighteen limb claims and emits one claim; leanVM's Flock reads no claim}\enspace{\small\textsf{\color{major}(major)}}\par\nopagebreak

A \code{FlockInterface} whose input is the eighteen claims and whose output is one weighted claim drops them, so with leanVM's verifier its knowledge-soundness error is 1.

\par\medskip\noindent\textbf{R17.}\enspace\textbf{Acceptance test 20 files a completeness failure under a soundness error, and attributes to the protocol an inverse only the Rust prover takes}\enspace{\small\textsf{\color{major}(major)}}\par\nopagebreak

The pinned Rust Flock prover derives a coefficient with \code{(1 + r)⁻¹} and at \code{r = 1} emits a proof its verifier rejects: an implementation completeness defect (probability at most \texttt{(\allowbreak{}k\_\allowbreak{}batch + 1)/\allowbreak{}|\allowbreak{}E|\allowbreak{}}), not part of \code{flockError}; the spine has no place for a completeness error.

\par\medskip\noindent\textbf{R18.}\enspace\textbf{The opening phase runs a sumcheck leanVM does not run}\enspace{\small\textsf{\color{major}(major)}}\par\nopagebreak
\fhead{Claim} After the one batching challenge \code{λ} the deployed prover's next message is the first round polynomial of WHIR's own sumcheck on \texttt{Σ\_\allowbreak{}x q(\allowbreak{}x)·W\_\allowbreak{}λ(\allowbreak{}x) =\allowbreak{} C\_\allowbreak{}λ}, interleaved with WHIR's commitments and closing on one equation; there is no reduction sumcheck and no evaluation of \code{q̃} (specification §8.5: ``there is no separate reduction sumcheck''). The blueprint's Layer 10 (a \code{μ}-round sumcheck on \code{W_λ·q} and a final evaluation query) followed by WHIR in place of the evaluation oracle has \code{μ} extra rounds and an extra scalar, so \texttt{verify\_\allowbreak{}iff\_\allowbreak{}compiled} cannot hold for Rust proofs.

\fhead{Claim} At both ArkLib pins \texttt{fiat\allowbreak{}Shamir\_\allowbreak{}completeness} is admitted and stated for a constant challenge oracle, Fiat–Shamir soundness is a \code{TODO}, round-by-round to state-restoration is commented out, \code{BCSTransform} is commented out, and \texttt{Commitment.\allowbreak{}extractability} has body \code{False}; the blueprint's ``each an ArkLib theorem to come'' is unfounded. gt-opening-compile adds that an interface quantified over all IOPPs with error \code{Q·max_i ε_i} is false (hash term, oracle messages, grinding), which would make the theorem vacuous, and that \#627 is a design issue, not a pull request.

\fhead{Claim} The sketch applies ArkLib's \texttt{Verifier.\allowbreak{}fiat\allowbreak{}Shamir} to an oracle verifier whose messages are the stack and the codewords in the clear: it would hash whole oracle messages, not Merkle roots; no \texttt{decode :\allowbreak{} Proof → messages} exists; the Merkle compilation, the grinding checks and the prover-chosen sizes are omitted.

\par\medskip\noindent\textbf{R22.}\enspace\textbf{Upstream Fiat–Shamir and BCS theorems will be about other constructions than leanVM's one-map BLAKE2s chain}\enspace{\small\textsf{\color{major}(major)}}\par\nopagebreak
\fhead{Claim} ArkLib's transforms use one random oracle on the full prefix or a duplex sponge, and the textbook BCS analysis uses independent oracles per role; leanVM uses one 64-byte BLAKE2s map for the chain, the untagged Merkle nodes and grinding. A chain lemma and a role-separation lemma are owed here.

\par\medskip\noindent\textbf{R23.}\enspace\textbf{The non-interactive error omits grinding, the list-size factor and the hash term, so it cannot carry leanVM's 128-bit claim}\enspace{\small\textsf{\color{major}(major)}}\par\nopagebreak
\fhead{Claim} leanVM's query rounds reach 128 bits only with 17 bits of grinding (the query rounds alone give about 111 bits), but \texttt{Fiat\allowbreak{}Shamir\allowbreak{}Security}'s error \code{Q·max_i ε_i} and \code{niError} have no proof-of-work factor, and no published theorem covers Fiat–Shamir with proof of work for multi-round IOPs; the commitment is list-binding only, so each oracle-protocol challenge costs \code{L_0·ε_i} after compilation (gt-opening-compile computes \code{L_0 ≤ 110} to \code{396} at level 0, up to \code{2^20} at the deepest levels); and the hash-collision term (\code{c·Q²/2^256}) is missing. \texttt{Σ piop\allowbreak{}Error < 2\textasciicircum{}-\allowbreak{}150} says nothing about the deployed security level, which the WHIR query rounds set.
\fhead{Evidence} blueprint \code{:1224}, \code{:1234-1235}, test 23; \texttt{whir\_\allowbreak{}config.\allowbreak{}rs:\allowbreak{}25-\allowbreak{}27,\allowbreak{} 36-\allowbreak{}38,\allowbreak{} 57-\allowbreak{}60,\allowbreak{} 537-\allowbreak{}568,\allowbreak{} 593-\allowbreak{}599}; \texttt{fiat\_\allowbreak{}shamir/\allowbreak{}src/\allowbreak{}lib.\allowbreak{}rs:\allowbreak{}30-\allowbreak{}51,\allowbreak{} 126-\allowbreak{}178}; \code{leaf.rs:108-118}; scratch \code{whir_params.py} (reproduces the Python query table); [CY24] Theorems 25.2.1, 31.3.1
\fhead{Proposed change} \code{niError Q} = \code{(Q + rounds)} × the largest per-challenge error of the compiled protocol (\code{L_0·ε_i} at oracle-protocol challenges, Theorem B.7's terms, \texttt{2\textasciicircum{}-\allowbreak{}17·(\allowbreak{}1−γ\_\allowbreak{}i)\textasciicircum{}(\allowbreak{}t\_\allowbreak{}i)} at ground query rounds) + the hash term; \texttt{Fiat\allowbreak{}Shamir\allowbreak{}Security} with grinding bits, the proof-of-work factor marked an assumption (literature.md §A.4; gt-opening-compile.md §I.7)

\par\medskip\noindent\textbf{R24.}\enspace\textbf{The list-binding compilation is a theorem the blueprint names and does not state}\enspace{\small\textsf{\color{major}(major)}}\par\nopagebreak
\fhead{Claim} The master theorems are about one committed \code{q}; the deployed commitment binds a \code{K}-valued interleaved word that may be close to up to \code{L_0} codewords over \code{E}. The compilation must prove that some list member satisfies every pooled claim (every member is \code{K}-valued and of the right size: a two-line argument not in the specification) with the oracle protocol's errors multiplied by \code{L_0}; none of \texttt{Fiat\allowbreak{}Shamir\allowbreak{}Security}, \code{BcsSecurity}, \code{McaJohnson} mentions the list.
\fhead{Evidence} \texttt{b-\allowbreak{}polynomial-\allowbreak{}commitment-\allowbreak{}scheme.\allowbreak{}tex:\allowbreak{}4,\allowbreak{} 70-\allowbreak{}72,\allowbreak{} 133-\allowbreak{}137}; \texttt{whir\_\allowbreak{}config.\allowbreak{}rs:\allowbreak{}593-\allowbreak{}599}; blueprint \code{:1190}, \code{:1296-1299}
\fhead{Proposed change} in Layer 12, the theorem of §E.3 (``List-binding compilation'') with its extractor (list-decode, select), state function, errors and two lemmas (gt-opening-compile.md §I.5)

\par\medskip\noindent\textbf{R25.}\enspace\textbf{The proof of work is the one verifier check no planned theorem or mutation makes load-bearing}\enspace{\small\textsf{\color{major}(major)}}\par\nopagebreak
\fhead{Claim} leanVM's 128-bit claim depends on grinding, yet the planned interfaces and Layer 12's six mutations leave it outside every theorem and test, together with truncated Merkle paths, digest canonicity and sizes above their caps.
\fhead{Evidence} blueprint \code{:1224}, \code{:1238-1240}; \texttt{fiat\_\allowbreak{}shamir/\allowbreak{}src/\allowbreak{}merkle.\allowbreak{}rs:\allowbreak{}22-\allowbreak{}37}
\fhead{Proposed change} restate the interface with grinding (R23); extend Layer 12's mutations (a wrong grinding nonce at each level, a truncated path, a nonzero third limb, a size above its cap) and run transcripts the specification rejects through the Rust and Python verifiers (literature.md §G.5)

\par\medskip\noindent\textbf{R26.}\enspace\textbf{Perfect completeness does not survive the Fiat–Shamir transform: the honest prover's grinding is a search}\enspace{\small\textsf{\color{major}(major)}}\par\nopagebreak
\fhead{Claim} The blueprint says perfect completeness survives the transform ``without any assumption''; the honest prover's grind loops over nonces with no bound, and no theorem says a nonce exists for every reachable chain state, so the Lean \code{prove} must be partial or fuelled. On the Flock exceptional point, §E.5 agrees with gt-flock-ring that the protocol is perfectly complete and the exceptional point is the Rust prover's.
\fhead{Evidence} \texttt{fiat\_\allowbreak{}shamir/\allowbreak{}src/\allowbreak{}lib.\allowbreak{}rs:\allowbreak{}126-\allowbreak{}155}; \texttt{Spine/\allowbreak{}Compose.\allowbreak{}lean:\allowbreak{}94-\allowbreak{}104}; blueprint \code{:1255-1257}
\fhead{Proposed change} \code{prove} takes fuel and returns \code{Option Proof}; \texttt{base\allowbreak{}Prover\_\allowbreak{}complete} is \texttt{prove … =\allowbreak{} some proof → verify … proof =\allowbreak{} true} (gt-opening-compile.md §I.6)

\par\medskip\noindent\textbf{R27.}\enspace\textbf{The base soundness (and completeness) theorems lack \texttt{Well\allowbreak{}Formed\allowbreak{}Bytecode}}\enspace{\small\textsf{\color{major}(major)}}\par\nopagebreak
\fhead{Claim} Layer 13's two base theorems are said to compose \texttt{constraint\allowbreak{}Soundness} and \texttt{constraint\allowbreak{}Completeness}, which require \texttt{Well\allowbreak{}Formed\allowbreak{}Bytecode prog}; a bytecode with a \code{JUMP} in the sentinel slot has steps that balance and no valid execution, so the soundness theorem is false without it.
\fhead{Evidence} blueprint \code{:222}, \code{:1247-1255}; \texttt{leanisa-\allowbreak{}blueprint.\allowbreak{}md:\allowbreak{}1156-\allowbreak{}1166}; \texttt{architecture.\allowbreak{}md:\allowbreak{}224-\allowbreak{}228}; \texttt{leanvm-\allowbreak{}target.\allowbreak{}md:\allowbreak{}57-\allowbreak{}62}; the proved test \texttt{tests/\allowbreak{}Leaner\allowbreak{}VMTests/\allowbreak{}Semantics/\allowbreak{}Execution.\allowbreak{}lean:\allowbreak{}415-\allowbreak{}461}
\fhead{Proposed change} add \texttt{(\allowbreak{}hwf :\allowbreak{} Well\allowbreak{}Formed\allowbreak{}Bytecode prog)} to both, or have \code{verify} decide the condition and reject (a technical decision for the orchestrator) (docs-debt.md §H.1; boundary-adaptor.md §G.3)

\par\medskip\noindent\textbf{R28.}\enspace\textbf{The base soundness theorem is not a probability statement about \code{verify}, and concludes no extracted witness}\enspace{\small\textsf{\color{major}(major)}}\par\nopagebreak
\fhead{Claim} ``Except with probability \code{niError}'' is attached to \texttt{verify prog input proof =\allowbreak{} true}, a decidable hypothesis about fixed values: there is no randomness in it. The theorem must be about a \code{Q}-query adversary against the random-oracle verifier with a straight-line extractor, the instantiation of the oracle by BLAKE2s being the one non-formal step, named; and its conclusion \texttt{∃ t,\allowbreak{} Valid\allowbreak{}Execution} is soundness for a language, dropping the extracted witness.
\fhead{Evidence} blueprint \code{:326}, \code{:1247-1248}; \texttt{architecture.\allowbreak{}md:\allowbreak{}264-\allowbreak{}273}; probe \code{Transport} (examples 3-4, old pins)
\fhead{Proposed change} the random-oracle statement with an adversary, its query log and the extractor, bounded by \code{niError Q}, plus the existential corollary and the pointwise \texttt{execution\_\allowbreak{}of\_\allowbreak{}extracted} (boundary-adaptor.md §G.3; gt-opening-compile.md §I.3, §E.1); the same repair in \code{architecture.md}

\par\medskip\noindent\textbf{R29.}\enspace\textbf{The base completeness theorem is false without resource hypotheses and needs a witness generator}\enspace{\small\textsf{\color{major}(major)}}\par\nopagebreak
\fhead{Claim} A valid execution may use \code{κ = 32}, whose four memory columns exceed the \code{2^28} stack the verifier accepts, and \texttt{Assignment\allowbreak{}Represents} fixes \code{κ}, so no accepted proof of that witness exists; ``witness of t'' needs the witness generator (T2), which the blueprint excludes; \texttt{constraint\allowbreak{}Completeness} takes \texttt{Well\allowbreak{}Formed\allowbreak{}Bytecode}, not \code{HasFillBlocks}; the rate is not chosen by the execution.
\fhead{Evidence} blueprint \code{:147-148}, \code{:1249-1250}, \code{:1255-1257}; \texttt{Semantics/\allowbreak{}Execution.\allowbreak{}lean:\allowbreak{}108-\allowbreak{}110}; \texttt{Arithmetization/\allowbreak{}Statement.\allowbreak{}lean:\allowbreak{}358}; \texttt{cpu/\allowbreak{}mod.\allowbreak{}rs:\allowbreak{}174-\allowbreak{}176}; \code{pcs.rs:51}; \code{verifier.py:1379}
\fhead{Proposed change} \texttt{base\allowbreak{}Prover\_\allowbreak{}complete} from a satisfying witness with admissible sizes and a valid rate, and \texttt{base\allowbreak{}Prover\_\allowbreak{}complete\_\allowbreak{}of\_\allowbreak{}execution} with a fit hypothesis \code{hfit}; ask leanISA for a minimal-height \texttt{constraint\allowbreak{}Completeness} (boundary-adaptor.md §G.4)

\par\medskip\noindent\textbf{R30.}\enspace\textbf{The instance is not \code{Ensemble.toM3} of the eight tables}\enspace{\small\textsf{\color{major}(major)}}\par\nopagebreak
\fhead{Claim} The memory and bytecode seed/finalize blocks and the state boundary must be boundary blocks whose index and program coordinates are \code{Coord.known} data of the instance (decision 8); with those blocks as tables of the instance the program would be committed, \code{M3Holds} would not imply the mixed witness's balance, and no adaptor theorem could be proved. No \texttt{Ensemble.\allowbreak{}to\allowbreak{}M3 :\allowbreak{} Ensemble → M3Instance} can exist (an instance needs \code{μ}, \code{layout}, public lines, \code{aux}, \code{Stmt}).
\fhead{Evidence} blueprint \code{:21}, \code{:77}, \code{:803-805}, \code{:1369}, \code{:1398}; \texttt{Spine/\allowbreak{}Instance.\allowbreak{}lean:\allowbreak{}86-\allowbreak{}98,\allowbreak{} 136}; \texttt{cpu/\allowbreak{}layout.\allowbreak{}rs:\allowbreak{}352-\allowbreak{}395}; \code{leaf.rs:453}; probe \code{KnownColumn} (exit 0, old pins; \code{KnownColumnNew} re-run at the new pins, passes)

\par\medskip\noindent\textbf{R31.}\enspace\textbf{No bridge lemma relates the boundary blocks to the Clean memory, bytecode and verifier rows}\enspace{\small\textsf{\color{major}(major)}}\par\nopagebreak
\fhead{Claim} \code{SatisfiedBy}'s balances range over all interactions, including the memory block's, the bytecode block's and the verifier's rows, which in the instance are boundary tuples; Layer 2's two bridges concern tables only, and nothing states that those rows' messages are the boundary tuples. \par\medskip\noindent\textbf{R32.}\enspace\textbf{The polynomial bridge of Layer 2 is noncomputable at the pin}\enspace{\small\textsf{\color{major}(major)}}\par\nopagebreak

\subsection{Disagreements between dossiers}\label{sec:reg-disagreements}

Where two dossiers disagree, each position is a row; the row's note names the other.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{R2} (The bus seam admits statements the deployed table sumcheck cannot serve): DISAGREEMENT with R3: gt-bus holds that the surplus generality costs nothing that matters. code-spine endorses gt-table-pub's redesign.
\item \textbf{R3} (The real bus phase can fill the spine's bus slot; the seam's surplus generality burdens only the table phase): DISAGREEMENT with R2: gt-table-pub and code-spine hold that the table phase which meets the seam must run checks leanVM does not run, so it is not the deployed verifier.
\item \textbf{R4} (The spine's completeness cannot carry an error, and Flock may need one): DISAGREEMENT with R17 (gt-flock-ring): there the specification's Flock is perfectly complete, only the Rust prover fails, so a Lean honest prover sending the true coefficients needs no completeness error. lib-arklib's own condition is answered by gt-flock-ring §4 and §8.12. The check of gt-flock-ring adds that ArkLib's completeness composition has side hypotheses (\code{hSeam}, completeness from every shared state). gt-opening-compile §E.5 agrees with gt-flock-ring that the exceptional point is the Rust prover's, and calls lib-arklib's error field ``the right insurance''.
\item \textbf{R7} (The GKR layer sumcheck is the normalized variant; the blueprint gives it the wrong degree, the wrong error and no definition): DISAGREEMENT with R8 on the GKR round error (4 against 5). The check corrected G1's wording on the table sumcheck: ``three of the cubic's four coefficients are sent'', not ``the whole cubic'' (verify-gt-bus.md §4 item 1).
\item \textbf{R8} (The GKR last-layer rounds cost \code{5/|E|} each, as the blueprint says): DISAGREEMENT with R7: gt-bus reads the check as made on the cofactor (normalized sumcheck), so the error is \code{4/|E|} and the blueprint's \code{5/|E|} is not tight. Both are upper bounds; neither dossier's conclusion on the zerocheck changes (the escape is a maximum with \code{ε_G ≥ 1/|E|} either way). Both agree on the combination challenges (\code{1/|E|} each) and on a zero error for the unused last combiner only in gt-bus.
\item \textbf{R17} (Acceptance test 20 files a completeness failure under a soundness error, and attributes to the protocol an inverse only the Rust prover takes): DISAGREEMENT with R4 (lib-arklib §G.2), which would give the spine a completeness error for Flock. The check notes that ``no verifier takes an inverse'' is literally false (constants are inverted); read ``no inverse of a challenge-dependent value''. gt-opening-compile §E.5 agrees that the exceptional point belongs to the pinned Rust prover.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Merged rows}\label{sec:reg-merged}

Rows that state one finding of two or more dossiers, with the dossiers each cites.
\begin{itemize}
